name: Staging AC Installation in Los Angeles Duplexes to Keep Units Livable

mainEntity.name: How can I stage AC installation in a Los Angeles duplex so one unit stays livable during construction?
mainEntity.text: How can I stage AC installation in a Los Angeles duplex so one unit stays livable during construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Staging AC installation in a Los Angeles duplex so one unit remains livable requires a clear phasing plan. Begin with a walkthrough to identify shared walls, attics, and electrical pathways that serve both units. Your goal is to isolate invasive work—like cutting registers, running linesets, and opening ceilings—to one side at a time. Schedule all major demolition, ductwork, and electrical rough‑in in the first unit while the other remains occupied, relying on existing fans or portable AC if needed. Ask the contractor to complete and commission the first system fully, including startup and preliminary testing, before moving to the second unit. This ensures at least one side has full cooling throughout most of the project. Coordinate any shared electrical panel or roof work to minimize outages and noise during early or mid‑day hours agreed with occupants. Communicate a detailed schedule to both households so they know when each phase will affect them. If inspections cover both systems, plan the sequence so the first completed side can still be used comfortably between inspection visits. Phased work may take longer overall, but it significantly reduces disruption and tenant frustration.
acceptedAnswer.description: To keep one side of a Los Angeles duplex livable during AC installation, plan a phased schedule: complete all noisy and invasive work in one unit first, use portable cooling if needed, coordinate line‑sets and electrical runs to avoid shared disruption, and only start the second unit once the first is operational and inspected.
